from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Same vector, different observers.", "GPS vs local hiker coordinates.", "Think of a cat on a rug."]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Viewpoint Shift", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.7)
        vector = Vector([1.5, 1.0], color=WHITE)
        cat = Dot(point=vector.get_end(), color=PINK)
        rug = Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE).rotate(PI/6)
        
        # Group them
        visuals = VGroup(axes, vector, cat, rug)
        self.place_in_area(visuals, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]), run_time=0.5)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(vector), run_time=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]), run_time=0.5)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(vector.animate.set_color("#FFD700"), run_time=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]), run_time=0.5)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(Create(rug), cat.animate.set_color("#00FF00"), run_time=1.0)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Basis as Building Blocks", 
                         ["Basis vectors are simple building blocks.", 
                          "Standard grid lines become skewed.", 
                          "Skewed grids represent new basis vectors."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show vector space basis vectors #FF4500.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF4500")
        
        # Create standard basis
        basis_i = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color="#FF4500")
        basis_j = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP, color="#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(basis_i, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(basis_j, "D3")
        self.play(Create(basis_i), Create(basis_j))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate vector spanning combination #1E90FF.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#1E90FF")
        
        # Transform into skewed
        skewed_u = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=2*RIGHT + UP, color="#1E90FF")
        skewed_v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=-RIGHT + UP, color="#1E90FF")
        
        self.play(
            Transform(basis_i, skewed_u),
            Transform(basis_j, skewed_v)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Label origin and basis vectors clearly #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        origin_label = Tex(r"O", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(origin_label, "E3")
        
        label_u = MathTex(r"\vec{u}", color=WHITE)
        label_v = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(label_u, "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(label_v, "C2")
        
        self.play(Write(origin_label), Write(label_u), Write(label_v))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Change of basis needs a translator.",
            "Matrix P holds new basis vectors.",
            "Old coordinates equal P times new.",
            "Use P to bridge perspectives.",
            "The translator bridges coordinate systems."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Change of Basis Matrix (P)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define P matrix
        P = MathTex(
            r"P = \begin{bmatrix} v_1 & v_2 \end{bmatrix}",
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_at_grid(P, 'C3', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Eq: [v]_old = P[v]_new
        eq = MathTex(
            r"[v]_{\text{old}} = P [v]_{\text{new}}",
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF8C00"))
        self.play(FadeIn(P))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))
        self.play(Indicate(P))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF1493"))
        self.play(Write(eq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF8C00"))
        self.play(Indicate(eq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Practical Application: Coordinate Conversion", [
            "Finding new coordinates requires matrix inversion.",
            "Inverse P un-skews the grid.",
            "Drone navigation uses this conversion.",
            "Back to global latitude/longitude.",
            "Calculate coordinates using inverse P."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        vec_text = MathTex(r"v_{custom} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}", color=WHITE)
        matrix_eq = MathTex(r"v_{global} = P^{-1} \cdot v_{custom}", color=YELLOW)
        result = MathTex(r"v_{global} = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}", color=GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Set up input vector coordinates #FFFFFF
        self.place_at_grid(vec_text, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(vec_text))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Inverse P un-skews the grid.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_eq, 'C3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_eq))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Drone navigation uses this conversion.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Back to global latitude/longitude.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(TEAL)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Calculate coordinates using inverse P.
        # Highlight final converted position #7FFF00 (Green)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(result, 'E4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(vec_text),
            FadeOut(matrix_eq),
            FadeIn(result)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Geometric Intuition", [
            "Perspective shift, not vector movement.",
            "Language changes, the object remains.",
            "Everything is a coordinate transformation."
        ])
        
        # Grid visual components
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        vector = Vector([1, 1], color=YELLOW)
        
        # Place on grid
        visual_group = VGroup(axes, vector)
        self.place_in_area(visual_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(visual_group)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Indicate vector to show object remains
        self.play(Indicate(vector))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        # Grid transformation to imply coordinate transformation
        self.play(axes.animate.apply_matrix([[1, 0.5], [0, 1]]))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Viewpoint Shift
sections.content: Introduce the concept that a vector remains constant, but its description depends on the 'observer' (basis). Use the analogy of a GPS coordinate system versus a hiker’s local relative directions (North/East vs. Forward/Left).
sections.example: A cat sits on a rug. Describing its position relative to the room's corners (standard basis) vs. describing its position relative to the rug's center (new basis).

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis as Building Blocks
sections.content: Briefly define a basis as a set of linearly independent vectors that span the space. Use a visual of grid lines for the standard basis {i, j} transforming into skewed, non-orthogonal grid lines for a new basis {u, v}.
sections.example: Visualizing the 2D plane: Show standard unit vectors (1,0) and (0,1) being replaced by arbitrary vectors (2,1) and (-1,1).

sections.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (P)
sections.content: Explain that to represent old coordinates in a new basis, we need a 'translator' matrix. This matrix P is formed by placing the new basis vectors as columns. Explain the equation [v]_old = P[v]_new.
sections.example: Representing a point (3, 2) in the standard basis as a linear combination of new basis vectors (e.g., v1=[2,1], v2=[1,2]).

sections.title: Practical Application: Coordinate Conversion
sections.content: Step-by-step calculation: Show how to find the new coordinates by multiplying the inverse of the matrix P by the original vector. Highlight the visual 'un-skewing' of the grid.
sections.example: A drone navigating in a 'custom' flight path grid: converting the drone's specific coordinate instructions back into the global latitude/longitude grid using the inverse matrix.

sections.title: Summary & Geometric Intuition
sections.content: Synthesize the concept: A change of basis is simply a perspective shift. Remind students that the vector hasn't moved; only our language to describe it has changed.
sections.example: A final 5-second animation showing a vector rotating on a grid while the grid lines themselves warp to reflect the new basis, keeping the vector's tip fixed in space.
